Patrick, thank you for trusting us with your shipping data.

I told you I would have something for you by Friday. This is it: your own ten months of labels, all 273,203 of them, run through our rating engine and laid out in a portal built for Savannah River Fulfillment.

We converted your heaviest parcel shipments to LTL and found these savings

About $55K a year

We grouped your labels into shipments (same building, same day, same ZIP). 5,886 of them total 150 lb or more. Most are still cheaper as parcel, because LTL has a minimum charge of about $300. 278 of them cost less as one LTL shipment, which is about 334 a year.

How a quote comes back

  • Your request reaches the HTL desk with a request number.
  • We rate it across our LTL carriers and drop any rate that expires before pickup.
  • You get each option with the carrier, transit time and your total.
  • Nothing is booked until you confirm an option.

Your requests

We priced your paid international labels with our international express partner. It is a small piece of your volume, and we can integrate it whenever you would like.

By destination group

Your file has no country column. Canada, the UK and Puerto Rico were identified from postal codes and quoted directly. The other groups use assumed rates, so a country column would firm them up. Estimates assume residential delivery and exclude duties and taxes.

How the parcel program works between SRF and HTL. Everything here is a proposal to discuss.

How the parcel program works between SRF and HTL. Everything here is a proposal to discuss.

How HTL is paid

  • $1.00 a package is built into the rate you pay.
  • 25% of the savings HTL delivers. SRF keeps 75%.
  • Full margin transparency: you see the partner rate, our margin and the share on every package.
  • The share is open for discussion.

Terms we propose

  • One-year review, no auto-renewal.
  • Numbers check-in every two weeks with both teams.
  • HTL holds and manages the carrier accounts and works billing issues for you.
  • You choose which client accounts move, and when.

Where every number in this portal comes from.

Your data

  • 273,203 labels from the ten monthly files you sent, January 2 to October 31, 2026, across three buildings.
  • "Cost today" is the label cost in your file. 30,711 labels have no cost in the file, so they are priced but not counted in savings.
  • Annual figures are the ten months scaled to twelve.

How a package gets priced

  • Ground packages of 25 lb or less and 30 in or less on the longest side are rated on our integration partner's rate card, by zone from the nearest injection point to each building.
  • Large light boxes are rated on dimensional weight.
  • A package only counts as moving if the new rate, with HTL's $1.00 included, is lower than what you pay today.
  • Packages outside the partner's current delivery ZIP list are held as "waiting on full network".

Not quoted and projected

  • Heavier parcel, the rest of the partner network and domestic air are not quoted yet. Air and expedited orders would only be quoted like for like on speed, so they stay with your current carriers for now. Their spend is shown as it is in your file, with no savings assumed.
  • The year-end outlook starts from your September and October average, or January to August if you choose it, and applies the peak lift you set. It is an estimate.

International and freight

  • Canada, the UK and Puerto Rico were quoted directly with our international express partner. Other destinations use assumed rates because the file has no country column.
  • Truckload, drayage and LTL shipments in this portal are samples. Nothing in those pages comes from your file.
  • All parcel figures are estimates from partner rate cards until rates are confirmed in writing.

You mentioned looking at more warehouse space. This page tests five central locations as a transloading warehouse: your inbound freight is cross-docked there, and orders for the middle of the country ship from it. It then replays a full year week by week so you can watch the lanes and the cost change.

Built on your data: 235,763 ground labels to the lower 48, January 2 to October 31, 2026. November and December are projected from your September and October pace.

How to read this: zones are estimated from straight-line miles between each building and the destination ZIP. The cost at a new zone comes from your own label costs by weight and zone.
